title: Kernel-affinity quantile sampler and telemetry playbook for FlashAttn v2/v3
text:
Kernel-affinity quantile sampler and telemetry playbook for FlashAttn v2/v3

description:
Objective: build a lightweight quantile-sampling-based kernel-affinity scorer and a corresponding telemetry/experimentation playbook to choose between FlashAttn v2, v3 and the fallback kernels per-tenant and per-shape. Motivation: recent sporadic regressions when automatically switching to v3 on certain long-tail token distributions (see incident INC-2025-09-attn-surge) require a principled, low-overhead decision layer that reduces oscillation and avoids P99 regressions while preserving v3 cost/throughput wins.

Scope and deliverables:
- Implement a kernel-affinity scorer that uses a streaming quantile summary of recent sequence-length and prefix-entropy statistics plus a per-tenant affinity prior to produce a ranked list of kernel candidates with confidence scores. The runtime will consult the scorer at prefill boundaries and during decoder warmup decisions.
- Telemetry plan: add new metrics (kernel_choice, affinity_score_quantiles, switched_for_reason, decision_confidence, downgrade_count) and dashboards for canary cohorts.
- A/B experiment harness and canary rollout strategy with deterministic warmup seeding for repros.
- Fallback and cooldown policy: when a candidate causes a latency or memory regression, apply a short exponential backoff and fall back to the highest-confidence compatible kernel.
- Regression test suite: microbenchmarks and replayed production traces covering headcounts, batch sizes, and long-context tails.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Quantile sampling (T-Digest style approx) was chosen over full histogram to keep memory per-tenant < 1KB and allow constant-time updates in the critical path. This trades off some accuracy on extreme tails but preserves throughput.
- Using a ranked candidate list (with confidence thresholds) allows deterministic fallback rules and avoids thrash that can happen with a single-point estimator.
- We intentionally keep the decision latency under 200 microseconds by caching affinity scores per-connection and only recomputing on significant distribution shifts (Kullback-Leibler divergence threshold).
- Privacy: per-tenant telemetry is aggregated; no raw input tokens are logged.

Instrumentation and artifacts:
- Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Kernel+Affinity+Quantile+Sampler (draft)
- GitHub feature branch and initial PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4827 (WIP)
- Canary dashboard (Grafana): /d/runtime/kernel-affinity-canary (adds kernel_choice and decision_confidence)
- Replay dataset: s3://redwood-prod-replays/2025-09-attn-surge-sample.tar.gz

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit and integration tests that validate the scorer under synthetic distributions (short/heady/long-tail) and produce deterministic ranking outputs.
- End-to-end canary demonstrating <= +5% median latency and <= +10% P99 vs baseline for >= 95% of requests in the cohort. Any cohort failing the P99 target must trigger auto-rollback in the harness.
- Telemetry surfaced and alerting on downgrade_count > 10/day for a tenant.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature gated behind runtime flag and tenant opt-in.
2) Internal rollout to dev tenants with replay testing (1 week).
3) Small production canary (5% of traffic across 3 instance pools) for 48 hours.
4) Evaluate telemetry and experiments; expand to 25% if stable, then to full opt-in.

Longer-term possibilities (out of scope for this ticket): global model-aware priors (per-model affinity), cross-tenant federated summaries to improve cold-start, and integrating with costs/quantization profiles.


comments:
2025-11-06 - Aisha Patel: Kickoff doc uploaded to Confluence and initial design sketched. Decided on streaming quantile summaries rather than histograms to limit memory. Action: Miguel to prototype scorer API and microbench it.
2025-11-08 - Miguel Torres: Prototype scorer implemented in C++ runtime module. Local microbench shows ~120us decision latency for cold compute and ~18us when cached per-connection. Pushed branch runtime/feat/kernel-affinity-sampler. PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4827
2025-11-10 - Emily Chen (SRE): Added Grafana panels for kernel_choice and decision_confidence. Hooked up canary alerts: P99 increase > 8% for canary triggers rollback. Need to add downgrade_count metric to the exporter.
2025-11-12 - Rohit Sinha (ML infra): Ran replay against 1M requests from the surge trace. Early results: v3 wins on median token throughput for 78% shapes, but for 12% of long-tail shapes P99 regressed by > 15%. The scorer ranked v3 lower for those shapes which is promising. Need to tune confidence thresholds to reduce false negatives.
2025-11-14 - Miguel Torres: Tuned KL divergence sensitivity from 0.02 to 0.005 to pick up subtle distribution shifts during decodes. Replays rerun, downgrade_count dropped by 30% in synthetic stress test.
2025-11-18 - Product review (Sana Li): Reviewed acceptance criteria and suggested adding a tenant-level opt-out toggle and a clear rollback playbook. Added ticket PM-411 to track the UI toggle work.
2025-11-19 - Miguel Torres: Addressed SRE feedback, exported downgrade_count and switched_for_reason tags. Updated PR with unit tests and bench harness; marking PR as Ready for Review.

acceptance_criteria:
Scorer returns deterministic ranked list for given seed distribution
Canary P99 within defined bounds for >=95% requests
Alerts fire for downgrade_count and decision_confidence anomalies
Unit + integration + replay tests pass in CI

notes:
Keep memory per-tenant <1KB for summaries
Avoid storing raw token data in telemetry
Decision path must be idempotent across failover to another instance

qa_plan:
Run replay on nightly 5M trace job with new scorer enabled for opt-in tenants
Smoke test canary to ensure no memory regressions under 400 concurrent connections
Run fault-injection test to ensure fallback triggers correctly on OOM or kernel errors
